INT_HASTE_1.actorText: Player-controlled Heroes and human Soldiers only

effectParams.description: Adds a dedicated rebindable Haste toggle whose default keyboard binding is H. Haste begins OFF. Pressing H while alive, player-controlled, and at positive Magic toggles Haste ON; pressing H again toggles it OFF. While Haste is ON and funded, HasteMovementMultiplier = 2.00 and applies to the actor's resolved voluntary locomotion speed after ordinary walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, MapOpenMovementMultiplier when applicable, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. Haste therefore doubles ordinary walking and ordinary Shift sprinting alike; it never replaces, consumes, disables, or changes access to the actor's normal sprint. HasteMagicDrainRate = CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate, using the same personal WIS-scaled utility-Magic rate as map viewing. Magic regeneration is suppressed while Haste is actively draining. Haste and map viewing are independent sustained Magic consumers: at base Haste, if both are active simultaneously, TotalUtilityMagicDrainRate = CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate + HasteMagicDrainRate = 2 × CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate. Reaching 0 Magic immediately turns Haste OFF and returns locomotion to its ordinary legal speed; death or loss of player control likewise ends the active Haste state. A map force-close caused by damage or map-Magic exhaustion ends only the map state and its map-open movement bonus; it does not itself toggle Haste OFF if Haste still has positive Magic. Haste changes no jump velocity, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, Push/knockback, falling, projectile motion, or forced movement.

All Haste toggle, normal-sprint preservation, regeneration-suppression, and zero-Magic termination rules remain unchanged.

Adds a private old-school synthetic GPS navigation assist with a dedicated rebindable toggle whose default keyboard binding is G. GPS starts enabled immediately when the feat is acquired. Acquisition displays a concise tooltip/system notice: GPS ENABLED — If it gets annoying, press G to turn it off. Press G again to turn it back on. Pressing the GPS action toggles the feature without spending Magic; every toggle plays a short electronic switch/chime and produces the ordinary bounded on-screen system notice GPS ON or GPS OFF. While enabled, GPS speaks after 1 second standing still without living enemies within 2 cells on the same floor, including enemies behind walls and human Soldiers. It repeats after a 4-second silence following each phrase. Movement, danger, combat or inactive states reset the trigger and cancel speech. Aim/facing may change while stationary. When triggered, GPS reads only the authoritative canonical route from the Hero's current cell to the currently active progression objective and emits one short 2000s/early-2010s-style direction assembled from a small fixed synthetic/concatenative voice bank. Supported phrase families include TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, TURN AROUND, CONTINUE FORWARD, IN N SQUARES TURN LEFT/RIGHT, IN N SQUARES TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, and YOU HAVE ARRIVED AT YOUR DESTINATION. N is derived from the contiguous legal route segment to the next turn, stair transition, or objective rather than guessed. GPS never invents a shortcut, predicts future progression stages, reveals enemies or loot, or performs a second pathfinding authority: it consumes the same canonical current-objective route used by ordinary navigation/breadcrumb logic. GPS is supplemental information and remains available even when lod_mapless 1 removes the visual minimap; it does not itself reveal a map or persistent route display. Active combat, death/spectating, staging, cutscenes, and other states where a navigation bark would be intrusive suspend the idle trigger. GPS has no Magic cost and does not alter Magic regeneration, BreadcrumbCells, movement, combat statistics, rewards, or objective logic.

While controlled by a human and wielding an equipped damage-dealing weapon, Killer Instinct remains dormant unless at least two living hostile actors are simultaneously inside the player's ordinary forward view and pass the same player-facing visibility/line-of-sight authority used for legal target identification. When that multi-hostile condition first becomes true and remains continuously true for 0.50 seconds, perform one target-priority evaluation; while it remains true, reevaluate no more than once every 1.00 second. If fewer than two valid hostiles remain, immediately clear the highlight and stop all Killer Instinct evaluation until the condition becomes true again; there is no general per-frame Think scan. Candidate discovery must reuse the existing visible/targetable hostile set or equivalent cached authority and may not iterate every world entity solely for this feat. For each valid candidate, compute a cheap deterministic EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot for one ordinary primary-fire trigger pull from the equipped weapon's current authored attack profile, using current deterministic attacker/target modifiers and mean damage-die values; do not roll dice, simulate Boom chains, predict future status procs, or Monte Carlo attacks. EstimatedShotsToKill = max(1, ceil(CurrentHP / max(1, EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot))). If one or more candidates have EstimatedShotsToKill = 1, select the one with the greatest EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot - CurrentHP kill margin; otherwise select the candidate with the lowest EstimatedShotsToKill. Break any remaining tie by lower CurrentHP, then stable actor ID. Render one red outline/halo tightly around the selected hostile model. The outline is informational only: it grants no aim assist, targeting lock, damage, AI-priority change, extra detection range, through-wall awareness, or tracking after ordinary visibility is lost, and it clears immediately when the target dies or becomes invalid.

While this feat is ready, the first incoming damage event tagged physical=true automatically receives PhysicalDamageReduction = max(0, WIS_MOD), applied once to the event's aggregated physical damage after ordinary damage dice/Boom resolution, CON DamageResistancePerDie, source-side scaling, and elemental/identity modifiers, but before Arcane Shield HP-to-Magic diversion, lethal intercepts, and final HP loss. Never reduce damage below 0. After an eligible physical event consumes the ready state, roll MindOverMatterCooldownSeconds = 3d4 seconds and do not apply Mind Over Matter again until that cooldown expires. These three d4 timing dice are sealed, non-damage utility dice and never explode or inherit Rogue damage-die mastery, DEX BoomShift, Wizard magical Boom rules, weapon-specific explosion rules, or other attack-die modifiers. When the cooldown expires, Mind Over Matter becomes ready again. Magical-only events with physical=false do not consume the ready state. A mixed physical=true/magical=true event may receive True Faith's magical reduction and, when Mind Over Matter is ready, Mind Over Matter's physical reduction on the same resolved event; each applies once and final damage is clamped at 0. Mind Over Matter does not alter Push, wall-slam damage, hit-stun, status saves, MagicSave, or any non-damage physical effect.

Sixth Sense grants three personal perception effects. First, the owner can visually perceive any entity whose authoritative state includes invisible=true. Invisibility is a reusable shared entity-state primitive rather than a Watcher-specific exception: Watchers use it now, and future enemies, effects, or actors may use the same state. An invisible entity is rendered only for the owning client as a clearly readable translucent silhouette/outline at its true current world position whenever that entity would otherwise satisfy ordinary world visibility and line-of-sight rules if invisibility were ignored. Second, Sixth Sense grants Nearby Hostile Sense: every living hostile entity on the owner's current floor whose cell-coordinate distance is within 2 grid cells is rendered to that owner as a readable through-geometry outline even when intervening walls or props block line of sight. For this sensor, NearbyCellDistance = max(abs(enemyCellX-ownerCellX), abs(enemyCellY-ownerCellY)); the effect applies when NearbyCellDistance <= 2 and floorId matches. This local 5x5-cell neighborhood intentionally ignores wall connectivity and closed-gate edges for perception only. Invisible hostiles within that neighborhood are also revealed by the same outline. Third, Sixth Sense grants Watcher Motion Sense: whenever a living Watcher is in its authoritative moving/locomotion state, each Sixth Sense owner on the same floor receives a private 3D positional Watcher movement sound attached to that Watcher's true current position. This cue plays whether the Watcher is visible or invisible and does not require line of sight; ordinary spatial attenuation provides direction and proximity, so a distant Watcher does not become an all-floor audio beacon. The cue starts when authoritative Watcher locomotion begins and stops when locomotion stops, the Watcher dies/despawns, the player changes floor, or Sixth Sense is no longer active. The movement sound is transmitted/rendered only for eligible Sixth Sense owners; players without the feat receive no such sound event. These effects create no minimap marker, breadcrumb, directional arrow, nameplate through the world, aim assistance, target lock, ballistic permission through geometry, AI aggro knowledge, or interaction permission. Sixth Sense never changes an entity's invisible state, cloak duration, AI/state machine, collision, targetability rules, or visibility to any other player; players without the feat perceive the entity normally. The server authoritatively determines feat ownership, invisible state, hostility, floor, cell coordinates, and Watcher locomotion state; owning clients render only authorized silhouettes and private Watcher movement audio. FeatDirector may offer Sixth Sense whenever the actor is an eligible cooperative hero; Watchers or any other invisibility-using enemy need not currently be present because the 2-cell hostile-sense effect is independently useful.

Warns about visible hostile monsters behind you and directly to either side. RearRangeCells = max(1, WIS_MOD), without Astral Reach. Quantize horizontal facing to the nearest cardinal maze direction. The rear footprint remains three cells wide for depths 1 through RearRangeCells: directly behind, plus one cell on either side of each rear cell. Add a single-cell-wide ray directly left and directly right from the player's current cell, each extending SideRangeCells = ceil(RearRangeCells / 2). No forward cells or other floors qualify. Closed walls, closed gates and ordinary blocking geometry still block detection. Retain the selected monster while it qualifies; otherwise choose by shortest footprint depth, then smallest absolute lateral offset, then stable actor identity. On acquisition or replacement after the prior selection ceases to qualify, name the monster in a private BEHIND YOU, LEFT or RIGHT notice in the live die-readout and Die Log, play a clearly audible alert, and briefly show a violet directional light toward its position at detection. The light is a transient directional notification, not an enemy outline, minimap marker or persistent tracker. Do not repeat the alert while the same selected monster remains qualified. No target lock, aim assist, combat bonus, through-wall detection or AI behavior change.
